How your AI agent can pay with your credit card, without ever holding it:

1. Your card stays stored in a trusted wallet.

2. When your agent goes to buy something, the wallet creates an agentic token: a stand-in card number that only works at that store, with limits like "don't spend more than $100."

3. Your agent hands the token to the store.

4. The store runs it through its usual payment processor, and the charge lands on your real card, with your rewards and card benefits intact.

"AOL was a helpful set of training wheels for getting everyone online, but the open web ultimately won. We think the same thing will happen with agents as well."

AI agents can now book the hotel and order the cleats, as long as they're allowed to pay.

That's set off the "wallet wars," with major players racing to connect to agents:

- Stripe's Link: 300M users
- Shopify's Shop Pay: 250M users
- PayPal: 400M+ users

How your agent pays matters. If a wallet pays the store with its own stand-in card, the purchase goes through, but your card rewards, purchase protections, and relationship with the store can get lost along the way.

Say your agent books a United flight on your airline credit card. If the wallet pays United with its own virtual card, the money moves, and your miles may never show up.

Agents also have to pick the right card for each purchase, and when one books the wrong hotel dates, someone has to make it right.

Where it's all headed: new open standards from Visa, Mastercard, and Amex.

"The best of all worlds is a future where my agent can use my credit card, without having my credit card."

Full piece from VGS's @terryangelos on the Wallet Wars: https://t.co/RvC0pSRjGH

The wallet wars are here.

Very Good Security chief strategy officer Terry Angelos joins a16z's Alex Rampell, his TrialPay co-founder from back in 2006 (TrialPay was later acquired by Visa), to discuss how agents are learning to spend money.

"Agents have all of a sudden become significantly more helpful and useful because they effectively have arms and legs, which are payment credentials."

VGS holds the payment credentials behind about 1/3 of all e-commerce, and now it's helping AI agents pay merchants. If you've bought anything online, there's a good chance VGS has already helped keep your card safe.

In the last three months, Terry says agents went from "spectators to actors." Once an agent has your payment credentials, it can book the piano teacher it previously could only find and recommend.

Now Stripe's Link, Shopify's Shop Pay, and PayPal are racing to connect to agents. It's all headed toward open standards from the card networks: agentic tokens that let an agent pay with your actual card.

VGS went from zero agentic tokens to a few million a week in three months.

"Agents have all of a sudden become significantly more helpful and useful because they effectively have arms and legs, which are payment credentials."

VGS holds the payment credentials behind about 1/3 of all e-commerce, and now it's helping AI agents pay merchants. If you've bought anything online, there's a good chance VGS has already helped keep your card safe.

In the last three months, Terry says agents went from "spectators to actors." Once an agent has your payment credentials, it can book the piano teacher it previously could only find and recommend.

Now Stripe's Link, Shopify's Shop Pay, and PayPal are racing to connect to agents. It's all headed toward open standards from the card networks: agentic tokens that let an agent pay with your actual card.

VGS went from zero agentic tokens to a few million a week in three months.
